title: Block vs Inline Elements 📏
description: Discover the two fundamental display behaviours that shape layouts.

slides.title: Two Types of Flow 🌊
slides.content:
# How Elements Behave Naturally

HTML elements come with a default display behaviour:
- **Block‑level elements** start on a new line and stretch to the full width available.
- **Inline elements** flow within the line and only take the space they need.

Understanding this is key to controlling layouts before you even write CSS.

quizData.question: Inline elements can never contain block elements.
quizData.explanation: By HTML rules, inline elements should not contain block elements. Doing so can cause unexpected layout issues.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## The `<div>` and `<span>` Workhorses

`<div>` is the generic block container; `<span>` is the generic inline container. Use them when no semantic tag fits, but prefer meaningful tags first.
